## Gastrointestinal Perforations

Across all studies included in the integrated safety dataset, a total of 2 participants who were on povorcitinib (0.1% of participants each in the povorcitinib total group for the All HS Population [Pool 2] and the All povorcitinib Population [Pool 3]) had a gastrointestinal (GI) perforation. One event was not an event of GI perforations but an event of cutaneous abscess on the abdomen, which was treated with a topical therapy. The event was miscoded during data collection for the Phase 2 study. The event of diverticulitis intestinal perforated was serious and occurred in a participant with demographic characteristics (obesity, age &gt; 60 years, and current alcohol use), medical history (hypertension), and prior and concomitant medications (ibuprofen and acetylsalicylic acid; pseudoephedrine hydrochloride) that may have been confounding factors for the event.

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

## Hypersensitivity Reactions

The overall incidence of hypersensitivity reactions for the Phase 3 HS Population (Pool 1) was low and similar in the povorcitinib total and placebo groups (0.4% in the povorcitinib total group and 1.2% in the placebo group). Urticaria in 3 participants (0.7%) and eye swelling in 2 participants (0.5%) in the placebo group were the most frequently reported hypersensitivity reactions; all other hypersensitivity reactions occurred in 1 participant each.

In the All HS Population (Pool 2), the overall incidence of hypersensitivity reaction events was low and identical between povorcitinib and placebo (1.1% in both groups). The exposure-adjusted incidence rate and study size- and exposure-adjusted incidence rate in the placebo group was higher compared with the povorcitinib total group (4.6 per 100 PY vs 1.1 per 100 PY). The most frequently reported hypersensitivity event was urticaria and incidence was similar between povorcitinib and placebo groups (0.5% vs 0.6). The exposure-adjusted incidence rate and study size- and exposure-adjusted incidence rate of urticaria in the placebo group was higher compared with the povorcitinib total group (2.8 per 100 PY vs 0.5 per 100 PY).

## Hidradenitis Suppurativa Exacerbations

The overall incidence of HS exacerbations for the Phase 3 HS Population (Pool 1) was similar in the povorcitinib total and placebo groups (1.1% in the povorcitinib total group and 1.5% in the placebo group).

The overall incidence of HS exacerbations in the All HS Population (Pool 2) was higher in the povorcitinib total group than the placebo group (5.8% in the povorcitinib total group and 1.5% in the placebo group).

Incidence rates provide additional context for understanding incidences of HS exacerbations in the clinical studies of povorcitinib in the All HS Population (Pool 2). After adjusting for study-size (5.8% and 1.5% in the povorcitinib total and placebo groups, respectively), IRs were higher for participants on povorcitinib compared with placebo. After adjusting for exposure (5.9 and 6.5 participants with the event per 100 PYs of exposure for the povorcitinib total and placebo groups, respectively) and exposure and study-size (5.9 and 6.6 participants with the event per 100 PYs of exposure for the povorcitinib total and placebo groups, respectively), IRs were similar for participants on povorcitinib and on placebo. The exposure- and study-size-adjusted IR of HS exacerbations for participants in the povorcitinib 75-mg without dose change group (6.5 participants with the event per 100 PYs of exposure) was higher compared with that for the povorcitinib 45-mg group (5.4 participants with the event per 100 PYs of exposure).

The incidence of HS exacerbations among participants who were treated with povorcitinib for 52 weeks or longer were 1.4% and 6.0% of participants in the placebo and povorcitinib total groups, respectively. The median time to onset of HS exacerbations for participants in the povorcitinib total group was 149.0 days for both the All HS Population (Pool 2) and the All Povorcitinib Population (Pool 3), and the conditional probability of a first event of HS exacerbation was lowest for participants on povorcitinib during Weeks 0 to 12 for the All HS Population and the All povorcitinib Population, and similar across all timepoints thereafter for both All HS and All povorcitinib Populations.

The integrated safety dataset; The AESI of HS exacerbations was reported by 91 participants (povorcitinib total: 83 participants, placebo: 8 participants). The majority of these events were considered by the investigator to be not related to study drug. Twenty-two participants had at least 1 event of HS exacerbation that was serious; most of which were Grade 3 or higher events. Eleven participants had AESIs leading to interruption of study drug, and 6 participants had AESIs leading to discontinuation of study drug. Most events had resolved by the data cutoff date; 35 of the 91

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

participants had unresolved AESIs at the time of data cutoff.

## Events of Clinical Interest

Several ECIs were predefined in the Phase 3 clinical development program. These events have been observed with other systemic JAK inhibitors and were selected for further safety monitoring.

The ECIs identified for the pivotal studies were the following: increased serum creatinine (&gt; 3 × ULN or &gt; 3 × baseline) and renal dysfunction; hepatic events and increased hepatic transaminases (&gt; 3 × ULN); increased creatine phosphokinase (&gt; 5 × ULN) and acne.

## Acne

Across all pools, the incidence of acne (PT) was higher in those participants who took povorcitinib than in those who took placebo, with the largest difference in Pool 2 (povorcitinib total: 20.4%, placebo: 4.3%). All acne events were Grades 1 or 2, and ≤ 0.5% of participants discontinued due to the event of acne.

## Deaths

At the time of data cutoff, there were 4 TEAEs with fatal outcomes reported across the povorcitinib development program.

The following is a summary of the 4 participants who had TEAEs with fatal outcomes:

- In Study INCB 54707-301, 1 participant in the povorcitinib 45-mg group died during the extension period. The participant had a medical history significant for obesity (), type 2 diabetes mellitus with poor glycemic control (HbA1c: 8.5%), hypertension, sleep apnea, asthma, chronic pain, neuropathy, and psychiatric illness. Their history also included multiple prior surgeries for HS and a family history of sudden death. The participant was an active

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

- smoker. The participant's concomitant medications at the time of the event included insulin, opioids, antihypertensives, antiepileptics, and psychotropics. In the months prior to the event, the participant had undergone surgery for their foot fracture with cast placement, followed by a period of immobilisation. Soon after, while still casted on the leg, the participant experienced a second fall and fractured their fibula and tibia. The participant was hospitalised for care of the fracture but did not receive standard antithrombotic therapy despite prolonged immobilisation. The participant was discharged home 2 weeks later. Shortly after discharge, the participant was found deceased at their home. The cause of death was underdetermined, and no autopsy was done. The event was considered by the investigator to be not related to study drug.
- In Study INCB 54707-204, 1 participant in the povorcitinib 75-mg with dose change group died after completing the study. The participant took povorcitinib 45 mg throughout the PC period (Day 1 through Week 16), povorcitinib 75 mg throughout the OLE period (Weeks 16 to 52), and povorcitinib 75 mg throughout the LTE period until completing the last day of study drug on Day 700. On Day 718, the participant was diagnosed with Stage 4 metastatic breast cancer (TEAE of metastatic neoplasm). The participant's condition continued to worsen, the participant was hospitalised, and following multiple treatment efforts and procedures, the participant died on Day 746. The event was considered by the investigator to be not related to study drug.
- In Study INCB 54707-206, 1 participant in the povorcitinib 15-mg group died during the PC period. The last dose of study drug prior to the fatal TEAE was on Day 10. The participant with a medical history of hypertension, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, obesity (BMI: 48.7 kg/m 2 ), and smoking, was found deceased in their residence on Day 13. The investigator confirmed that the approximate date that the participant passed away was Day 11 (TEAE of death). The cause of death was unknown. An autopsy was not performed. The event was considered by the investigator to be not related to study drug.
- A participant in the 75-mg without dose change group had a fatal TEAE of myocardial infarction during the extension period of Study INCB 54707-207. The participant's relevant medications taken prior to the event included atorvastatin, isosorbide dinitrate, and sildenafil citrate, and their relevant concomitant medications included atorvastatin, epinephrine, and amiodaron. The participant had ongoing hypercholesterolemia. The screening and Week 12 ECGs showed sinus bradycardia (48 and 58 bpm, respectively). No evidence of hypertension was noted at Week 12. The last dose of study drug prior to the fatal TEAE was on Day 113. On Day 114, while traveling abroad, the participant's partner was awakened by the participant's irregular breathing, described as \"agonal and not normal.\" Emergency services was contacted and attempted cardiopulmonary resuscitation. The attempts were unsuccessful, and the participant died. The provisional cause of death was cardiac arrhythmia due to myocardial infarction. An autopsy was not performed, limiting further causality determination. The event was considered by the investigator to be not related to study drug and was considered more plausibly attributed to underlying cardiovascular risk factors, specifically hypercholesterolemia.

## 5.4.5 Discontinuation due to adverse events

## Adverse Events Leading to Study Drug Discontinuation

Phase 3 Hidradenitis Suppurativa Placebo-Controlled Population (Pool 1)

Study drug discontinuation in participants in the Phase 3 HS PC Population was reported in 31 participants (3.8%) in the povorcitinib total group and 7 participants (1.7%) in the placebo group. The TEAEs that led to study drug discontinuation in more than 1 participant included acne (3 participants in the povorcitinib 75-mg group) and ALT increased (2 participants in the povorcitinib 45-mg group), and anaemia (2 participants in the povorcitinib 45-mg group). All remaining TEAEs leading to study drug discontinuation were reported by no more than 1 participant each. Other TEAEs leading to study drug discontinuation included abdominal pain upper, acne cystic, aspartate aminotransferase increased, colitis, constipation, dizziness, drug eruption, drug hypersensitivity, electrocardiogram QT prolonged, epilepsy, fatigue, gamma-glutamyltransferase increased, headache, hidradenitis, liver injury, mouth ulceration, neutropenia, osteonecrosis, platelet count decreased, pyoderma gangrenosum, scrotal oedema, syncope, thrombocytopenia, weight increased, arthritis, breast cancer, cellulitis, hypertension, and viral infection. The majority of events that led to study drug discontinuation were Grade 1 or 2.

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

## All Hidradenitis Suppurativa Population (Pool 2)

In the All HS Population, with inclusion of safety data from the Phase 2 HS studies and the extension periods of the Phase 3 studies and Study INCB 54707-312 (Cohorts B and C), the incidence of TEAEs leading to study drug discontinuation were reported in 121 participants (8.55%) in the povorcitinib total group and 11 participants (2.4%) in the placebo group. The most commonly reported TEAEs leading to study drug discontinuation in more than 2 participants who took povorcitinib included anemia (n=17), acne (n=7), ALT increased (n=6), hidradenitis (n=6), pulmonary embolism, transaminases increased, and weight increased (n = 3 each). All remaining TEAEs leading to study drug discontinuation were each reported by no more than one or two participants. The majority of events that led to study drug discontinuation were Grade 1 or 2.

## Adverse Events Leading to Study Drug Interruption

## Phase 3 Hidradenitis Suppurativa Placebo-Controlled Population (Pool 1)

The types of TEAEs leading to interruption of study drug in participants in the Phase 3 HS PC Population were consistent with the types of events that were observed in the Phase 3 HS PostAnti-TNF Population, 58 participants (7.12%) in the povorcitinib total group and 24 participants (5.9%) in the placebo group. The most frequent TEAEs leading to interruption of study drug (≥ 2 participants in any treatment group) were COVID-19, hidradenitis, blood creatine phosphokinase increased, herpes zoster, ALT increased, AST increased, hemoglobin decreased, nasopharyngitis, platelet count decreased, and UTI. The majority of events that led to study drug interruption were Grade 1 or 2.

## All Hidradenitis Suppurativa Population (Pool 2)

In the All HS Population, with inclusion of safety data from the Phase 2 HS studies, the extension periods of the Phase 3 studies, and from the treatment-extension study (INCB 54707-312), the incidence of TEAEs leading to interruption of study drug was reported in 262 participants (18.4%) in the povorcitinib total group and 27 participants (5.8%) in the placebo group. The most frequent TEAEs leading to interruption of study drug (≥ 5 participants in any treatment group) were blood creatine phosphokinase increased, COVID-19, anemia, herpes zoster, upper respiratory tract infection, ALT increased, haemoglobin decreased, AST increased, and hidradenitis. The majority of events that led to study drug interruption were Grade 1 or 2.

## Use in Pregnancy and Lactation

No adequate and well-controlled studies of povorcitinib have been conducted in pregnant females to inform drug-associated risks. Females who were pregnant or lactating were excluded from all clinical studies. Females of childbearing potential were required to use effective contraception, and men must have been willing to abide by protocol-specified methods throughout the study to avoid fathering a child.

A total of 21 pregnancies have been reported across the povorcitinib clinical development program as of the data cutoff date. (Table 87).

## 5.4.8 Safety related to drug-drug interactions and other interactions

## Drug Interactions

Povorcitinib is primarily cleared by CYP3A4 metabolism. Therefore, a DDI study (INCB 54707-104) was conducted to assess the effect of an established CYP3A4 inhibitor or inducer on the PK of povorcitinib. Study INCB 54707-104 evaluated the effect of itraconazole (CYP3A4 inhibitor), rifampin (CYP3A4 inducer), and esomeprazole (proton pump inhibitor) on the PK of povorcitinib. Results from this study showed that both itraconazole and rifampin had a significant impact on the PK of povorcitinib. Therefore, for patients receiving chronic treatment with strong systemic CYP3A4 inhibitors, the recommended dose is 45 mg once daily. Patients should be monitored for changes in disease activity if povorcitinib is co-administered with moderate systemic CYP3A4 inducers. There was no impact of esomeprazole on the PK of povorcitinib.

Another DDI study (Study INCB 54707-111) was performed to evaluate the effect of multiple doses of povorcitinib on the PK of a single dose of combined oral contraceptive containing LNG and EE. Coadministration of povorcitinib with LNG + EE did not have a significant impact on the PK of LNG or EE; therefore, no dose adjustment is required for LNG 0.15 mg + EE 0.03 mg when coadministered with povorcitinib.

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

Finally, a third DDI study (Study INCB 54707-110) was performed to assess the effect of single or multiple doses of povorcitinib on the PK of digoxin, rosuvastatin, and metformin and the effect of multiple doses of probenecid on the PK of povorcitinib. Overall results suggest no impact of povorcitinib on metformin AUCs but a slight reduction in Cmax when they are coadministered. The effect of povorcitinib on exposures of digoxin, rosuvastatin, and metformin were not considered clinically significant. Overall results suggest no clinically relevant impact of probenecid on povorcitinib exposure when they are coadministered.

## Vital signs, physical findings, and other observations related to safety

Vital Signs

Most participants had normal vital signs at baseline and at post dose timepoints, and there were no meaningful trends in changes in vital signs over time. TEAEs of vital signs that led to study drug interruption or discontinuation were isolated events.

## Electrocardiograms

INCB 54707-107 was a randomised, partially double-blind, placebo- and positive-controlled, parallel-group study to evaluate the effect of therapeutic and supratherapeutic doses of povorcitinib on ECG parameters, including the QTc, in healthy participants. No QT prolongation was seen (for details, see section on Clinical pharmacology).

Not applicable

## 5.4.12 Overall discussion and conclusions on clinical safety

## 5.4.12.1 Discussion

## 5.4.12.1.1 Overall assessment of available safety data

## Safety data collection

Exposure and safety data were analysed for 5 pooled populations: Phase 3 HS PC Population (Pool 1), Phase 3 HS Post-Anti-TNF PC Population (Pool 1b), All HS Population (Pool 2), All HS Post-Anti-TNF Population (Pool 2b), All povorcitinib Population (Pool 3). The pooling strategy includes Phase 3 HS Post-Anti TNF PC Population (Pool 1b) from the PC period of the pivotal Phase 3 studies, which is the target population for the proposed indication. Data were also adequately collected from a broader PC HS patient pool (Pool 1) as well as from during longer povorcitinib exposure periods that include phase 2 studies and the ongoing treatment extension study (INCB 54707-312) for the All HS PostAnti TNF Population (Pool 2b) and the All HS Population (Pool 2).

Overall, the pooling strategy is considered appropriate for the safety analyses in the intended indication (post-anti-TNF HS) as Pool 1b safety analyses are placebo-controlled. Importantly, safety is also analysed in broader HS participant pool during PC controlled period (Pool 1) as well as in both post-anti-TNF and all HS participants with longer duration of povorcitinib exposure (Pool 2b and Pool 2, respectively). Analyses include also vitiligo and PN studies (Pool 3), which increases the magnitude of the overall duration of exposure and the numbers of participant-years. This strategy adequately enhances the likelihood of identifying less common yet potentially clinically important TEAEs. For the pooled analyses, TEAEs reported in each study have been appropriately coded using MedDRA and the safety data collection plans have satisfactorily addressed the influence of intrinsic and extrinsic factors.

## Patient exposure

Data for safety analyses are available from 1850 participants, who have received at least 1 dose of povorcitinib, evaluated in 9 studies (INCB 54707-202, -203, -204, -205, -206, -207, -301, -302, and -312) across three indications (HS; PN, vitiligo and CSU). The data cut-off date for analyses of pivotal phase 3 studies was 03 February 2025 for study INCB 54707-301 and 07 January 2025 for study INCB 54707-302, when all participants had completed the primary endpoint (Week 12). The final CSRs for the pivotal studies were submitted by the applicant upon CHMP's request (LPLVs were 23 December 2025 and 21 November 2025, respectively). The cut-off date for study INCB 54707-312 was 21 November 2025.

In general, the demographics and other background factors, including prior and concomitant medications were balanced between PBO and povorcitinib participants in all 5 pools.

It is noted that the exposures for the intended indication population, i.e. HS Post-Anti-TNF PC Population (Pool 1b and Pool 2b) are somewhat restricted and less than the ICH recommendation of over 6 months and over one-year exposures for safety analyses. Nevertheless, this is not considered to be an issue for the overall safety assessment as there is sufficient exposure in all HS participant pools 1 and 2.

In total 1850 participants have been exposed to povorcitinib during the clinical studies. In the HS studies (Pool 2), 644 participants have been exposed to the 45 mg dose and 996 participants to the 75 mg dose. In pool 2, 474 and 767 HS-patients have received povorcitinib 45mg and 75mg, respectively, for ≥ 6 months; the corresponding figures for ≥ 1 year are 260 (45mg) and 680 (75mg). The long-term exposure is considered adequate for safety analyses.

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

Collectively, the presented exposure levels and patient years in different pools are sufficient for reliably assessing the safety of povorcitinib in HS as they also include satisfactory numbers of patients with extended exposure periods.

## Overall Summary of Adverse Events

Placebo controlled (PC) period: In the Phase 3 HS Post-Anti-TNF PC Population (Pool 1b) and in the Phase 3 HS PC Population (Pool 1), the overall incidence of TEAEs was lower in participants in the placebo group than in those who received povorcitinib. The incidence of Grade 3 or higher TEAEs was low and comparable to PBO. Also, relatively few participants had serious TEAEs. Similarly, TEAEs leading to study drug interruption or discontinuation remained at comparable levels to PBO.

In conclusion, during the PC period, the overall safety profile observed in the Phase 3 HS Post-AntiTNF PC Population (Pool 1b) was largely consistent with the broader population studied in the pivotal studies (Pool 1) through Week 12. Importantly, there were more treatment-associated TEAEs in the povorcitinib groups compared to PBO with the highest numbers in the povorcitinib 75mg recipients. In contrast, the incidences of serious TEAEs and TEAEs leading to interruption or discontinuation of the study drug were comparable to PBO in povorcitinib participants.

Long term exposure data: In all HS population (pool 2) there were numerically more TEAEs in povorcitinib participants vs PBO. Also, the incidence of treatment-related TEAE was higher in povorcitinib participants. There were also more Grade 3 or higher TEAEs and serious TEAEs in povorcitinib group. More povorcitinib recipients also discontinued the study drug and there were more study interruptions in participants receiving povorcitinib. Further, with the inclusion of the safety data from the extension period of the pivotal studies and data from the treatment-extension study (INCB 54707-312) in Pool 2b, a higher proportion of participants in the povorcitinib total group compared to Pool 1b (Phase 3 HS Post-Anti-TNF PC Population) experienced Grade 3 or higher TEAEs, serious TEAEs, and TEAEs leading to drug discontinuation.

It is noted that the All HS Post-Anti-TNF Population (Pool 2b) and the All HS Population (Pool 2) include HS clinical studies, which have PC periods with a protocol-defined length followed by considerably longer extension or OLE and LTE periods in which participants are exposed to povorcitinib only. However, the highest percentages of aforementioned TEAEs were typically seen in participants with 75mg dose compared to 45 mg dose, which suggests a relation to the study drug. In contrast, when the analyses were focused to those HS participants in pool 2 who had received povorcitinib 52 weeks or longer there were similar numbers of treatment-related TEAEs in 75mg (without dose change) compared to the 45 mg group, which indicates that the long-term use does not cause a dose-dependent increase in the treatment associated TEAEs.

In conclusion, the overall safety profile remained consistent with extended treatment beyond the PC period and is consistent between the safety pool 2b (post-anti-TNF HS) and pool 2 (all HS).

## Common adverse events

Placebo controlled period: The most common TEAE in participants who took povorcitinib was acne in the PC period of pivotal studies. In both PC pools, the other more frequently reported TEAEs by PT in participants who took povorcitinib compared to PBO included nasopharyngitis, fatigue, headache, COVID-19, and upper respiratory tract infection. These TEAEs were in general more frequently observed in participants with the higher, 75mg dose. Few participants had Grade 3 or higher TEAEs in the Phase 3 HS PC population and there was no difference between PBO and total povorcitinib group.

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

Collectively, these data indicate that several TEAEs during PC period may be treatment-related and povorcitinib dose-dependent.

Long term exposure data: In the All Hidradenitis Suppurativa Post-Anti-TNF Population (Pool 2b), the proportion of participants who had at least 1 TEAE was greater in the povorcitinib total group than in the placebo group. The most frequently reported TEAEs among participants in the Pool 2b were consistent with those observed for the Phase 3 HS Post-Anti-TNF PC population (Pool 1b) with acne being reported in more participants in the povorcitinib total group than the placebo group. In general, the findings regarding the most common TEAEs in all HS population (Pool 2) and all povorcitinib (pool 3) safety analyses were largely consistent with Pool 2b.

In the pools with longer exposure data, no new safety signals appeared in comparison to the PC participant pools when the analyses were restricted to TEAEs with higher or equal than 2% incidence, with the exception of more hidradenitis and increased blood creatine phosphokinase TEAEs in povorcitinib participants. These and more rare safety findings are further discussed below.

## Adverse Events of Special Interest

Adverse Events of Special Interest were selected due to their relevance for safety monitoring in chronic inflammatory diseases across the JAKi class and regulatory feedback. The applicant's strategy regarding the selection of AESI is endorsed.

Serious Infections: In Pool 1 there were 6 serious infections in the PBO group (1.5%) and 2 in the total povorcitinib group (0.2%). In pool 2, 7 serious infections were observed in the PBO group (1.5%) and 26 in the total povorcitinib group (1.8%). The incidence of serious infections remained low during 52 weeks or longer use of povorcitinib, n=12 (1.7%) in the total povorcitinib group. Overall analyses of serious infection described a low incidence and no clear pattern of increasing risk with longer exposure. The observed data do not indicate a clear dose-related increase in serious infections. Importantly, the wording in SmPC section 4.4 has been updated to explicitly acknowledge the occurrence of serious infections and to align the warning text with that of other JAKis involved in the Article 20 referral. In addition, in view of the important potential risk of serious infection, active serious systemic infections, including active tuberculosis was added as a contraindication in SmPC section 4.3, which is also in line with this class of medicinal products.

Opportunistic Infections: Based on the updated safety dataset, opportunistic infections were uncommon in the povorcitinib groups and no clear treatment-related signal or dose/dependency trend is described. In the All HS Population, the exposure-adjusted incidence rate and study size- and exposure-adjusted incidence rate in the povorcitinib total group were each 0.5 per 100 PY, which is lower than the observed background rate in HS. 9 events of oral candidiasis were observed among povorcitinib participants (1 in 15 mg, 5 in 45 mg, 3 in 75 mg group) whereas none were reported in the placebo group. None of the events were considered SAEs. However, the candidiasis events did not increase during longer treatment and among the observed cases, there were predisposing factors such as inhaled corticosteroids and active smoking, therefore the oral candidiasis is not considered as an ADR at present time.

Serious and opportunistic infections will also be further characterised in the post-marketing setting (i.e. category 3 PASS, see RMP section).

Herpes Zoster: Herpes zoster AESIs were reported by 41 participants in integrated safety dataset (40 participants in the povorcitinib total group and 1 participant in the placebo group). Of these, 20 participants had herpes zoster AESIs that were considered by the investigator to be related to the study drug. None of these herpes zoster AESIs were serious TEAEs; all were Grades 1 and 2 in severity. HZ is appropriately included in the SmPC section 4.4. 'viral reactivation' and section 4.8 as an ADR with a frequency uncommon. In addition, herpes zoster is included as an important identified risk in the RMP and will be further characterised in the post-marketing setting (i.e. category 3 PASS, see RMP section). Tuberculosis: There were no treatment-emergent AESIs related to tuberculosis at the time of data cutoff. A warning on tuberculosis is added in SmPC section 4.4 recommending patients to be screened for TB before starting povorcitinib therapy and includes a cross-reference to the contraindication in patients with active TB as well as the need to consider anti-TB therapy prior to initiation of povorcitinib in patients with previously untreated latent TB or in patients with risk factors for TB infection. Patients should also be monitored for the development of signs and symptoms of TB. Malignancies: In the analyses of the integrated safety dataset malignancies were observed in 9 participants (povorcitinib total: 7 participants, placebo: 3 participants). All AESIs of malignancy were considered by the investigator as not related or unlikely related to the study drug. The incidence of malignancies among participants who were treated for 52 weeks or longer were as follows: 0.0% and 1.0% of participants in the placebo and povorcitinib total groups, respectively. Due to limited amount of long-term safety data, firm conclusions on the relationship between povorcitinib and malignancies cannot be drawn. Importantly, similarly to other JAKis, SmPC section 4.4. correctly acknowledges that malignancies and NMSCs have been reported in patients receiving povorcitinib. In line with the Article 20 referral for JAK inhibitors authorised in chronic inflammatory disorders, in patients with malignancy risk factor, povorcitinib should only be used if no suitable treatment alternatives are available. Periodic skin examination is recommended for all patients, particularly those who are at increased risk for skin cancer. In addition, malignancy (excluding non-melanoma skin cancer (NMSC)) and NMSC are included as important potential risks in the RMP and will be further characterised in the post-marketing setting (i.e. category 3 PASS, see RMP section). Cardiovascular Events (MACE): In the integrated safety dataset, 3 participants had cardiovascular (MACE) events. One participant in the povorcitinib group had a Grade 3 AESI of acute myocardial infarction. This patient had other risk factors that likely contributed to the event and thus the investigator considered the AE unlikely related to the study drug. One participant in the povorcitinib group in the Phase 2 CSU study had a Grade 5 AESI of myocardial infarction, the event was independently assessed by both sponsor and investigator as not related to study drug. One participant in the povorcitinib group in a Phase 3 HS study had a TEAE of Grade 4 ischemic stroke that led to interruption of study drug and was reported as resolved with sequalae. The investigator considered the event to be related to study drug. Given the absence of objective evidence of ischemia and the participant's substantial underlying risk factors for vascular events (severe obesity and active smoking), the sponsor considered the reported event not suspected to be related to povorcitinib. The SmPC appropriately acknowledges in section 4.4 that MACE has been observed in patients receiving povorcitinib. In line with the Art 20 referral for JAK inhibitors, in patients with CV risk, povorcitinib should only be used if no suitable treatment alternatives are available. In addition, MACE is included as an important potential risk in the RMP and will be further characterised in the post-marketing setting (i.e. category 3 PASS, see RMP section). Other Embolic and Thrombotic Events: In the integrated safety dataset, embolic and thrombotic events were reported by 12 participants in the povorcitinib total group. There were no embolic or thrombotic events during the PC period (Pool 1 and 1b). Notably, HS patients have elevated risk for venous thrombosis and the observed incidence remains below the expected background in evaluations beyond the PC period. Due to limited amount of long-term safety data, firm conclusions on the relationship between povorcitinib and embolic/thrombotic events cannot be drawn. SmPC acknowledges that these events have been reported in patients receiving povorcitinib, and the warning text has also been aligned with other JAK inhibitors recommending to use povorcitinib with Assessment report caution in patients with known VTE risk factors other than cardiovascular or malignancy risk factors. In addition, the warning also recommends to periodically re-evaluate patients during povorcitinib treatment to assess for changes in VTE risk and to discontinue povorcitinib in patients with suspected VTE, regardless of dose. In addition, VTE is included as an important potential risk in the RMP and will be further characterised in the post-marketing setting (i.e. category 3 PASS, see RMP section). Gastrointestinal Perforations: Gastrointestinal (GI) perforations were reported in 2 participants during the povorcitinib studies. One event was not an event of GI perforations but an event of cutaneous abscess on the abdomen, which was treated with a topical therapy. The event was miscoded during data collection for the Phase 2 study. The event of diverticulitis intestinal perforated was serious and occurred in a participant with demographic characteristics (obesity, age &gt; 60 years, and current alcohol use), medical history (hypertension), and prior and concomitant medications (ibuprofen and acetylsalicylic acid; pseudoephedrine hydrochloride) that may have been confounding factors for the event. HS is not independently recognised as a risk factor for GI perforation. Given the rarity of the events and the younger demographic profile of patients with HS who generally have a lower baseline prevalence of the risk factors for GI perforation, the applicant's proposal to closely monitor GI perforation in future PSURs and update the RMP in the post-marketing setting as appropriate based on emerging post-marketing data is agreed (also see RMP). Hypersensitivity reactions: The overall incidence of hypersensitivity reactions for the Phase 3 HS PC Population (Pool 1) was low and similar in the povorcitinib total and placebo groups (0.4% and 1.2% for the povorcitinib total group and the placebo group). In the All HS Population (Pool 2), the overall incidence of hypersensitivity reaction events was low and identical between povorcitinib and placebo (1.1% in both groups). The exposure-adjusted incidence rate and study size- and exposure-adjusted incidence rate in the placebo group was higher compared with the povorcitinib total group (4.6 per 100 PY vs 1.1 per 100 PY). Hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1 is included as a contraindication in SmPC section 4.3. This is agreed. Hidradenitis Suppurativa Exacerbations: In the integrated safety dataset the AESI of HS exacerbations was reported by 91 participants (povorcitinib total: 83 participants, placebo: 8 participants). The majority of these events were considered by the investigator to be not related to study drug. In the analyses of all HS population (Pool 2), after adjusting for exposure (5.9 and 6.5 participants with the event per 100 PYs of exposure for the povorcitinib total and placebo groups, respectively) and exposure and study-size (5.9 and 6.6 participants with the event per 100 PYs of exposure for the povorcitinib total and placebo groups, respectively), IRs were similar for participants on povorcitinib and on placebo. It is agreed that given the natural history of HS, it is to be expected that patients may experience an exacerbation during the treatment period. Considering that the treatment periods were longer and exposures higher in the povorcitinib group, it can be concluded that the available data across povorcitinib clinical studies do not suggest an increase in the rates of HS exacerbation in participants with HS at present time.

## Events of Clinical Interest

Several ECIs events that have been observed with other systemic JAK inhibitors were predefined as ECIs: Increased serum creatinine (&gt; 3 × ULN or &gt; 3 × baseline) and renal dysfunction, Hepatic events and increased hepatic transaminases (&gt; 3 × ULN), Increased creatine phosphokinase (&gt; 5 × ULN) and acne. The selection of aforementioned events is endorsed. Laboratory component: Pool 1: during the PC period an increased creatine phosphokinase values were observed more frequently in povorcitinib participants (PBO: 7, 1.7%, 45mg 11, 2.7%, 75mg: 16, 3.9%). In the all HS participant pool 2 that included also longer exposure times, the trend in

increased creatine phosphokinase levels was confirmed (PBO: 3, 0.6%, 45mg: 28, 4.3%, 75mg without dose change 41, 4.4%.

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

AE component: In Pool 1, the event of alanine aminotransferase increased occurred in 0.5% of participants in the total povorcitinib group versus 0.0% in the placebo group (0.4% vs 0.0 in Pool 1b) and aspartate aminotransferase increased occurred in 0.5% of participants in the total povorcitinib group versus 0.0% participants in the placebo group (0.4% vs 0.0% in Pool 1b). In Pool 2, the event of alanine aminotransferase increased occurred in 2.4% of participants in the total povorcitinib group versus 0.0% in the placebo group; aspartate aminotransferase increased occurred in 1.4% of participants in the total povorcitinib group versus 0.0% participants in the placebo group; and transaminases increased occurred in 0.6% of participants in the total povorcitinib group versus 0.0% in the placebo group. The elevated creatine phosphokinase levels are appropriately included in SmPC section 4.8 as an ADR. Upon CHMP's request, the applicant has appropriately included elevated liver transferases as an ADR in SmPC 4.8 (\"Alanine aminotransferase increased &gt;3×ULN, uncommon\" and \"Aspartate aminotransferase increased &gt;3×ULN, uncommon).

Acne: Across all pools, the incidence of acne (PT) was higher in those participants who took povorcitinib than in those who took placebo, with the largest difference in Pool 2 (povorcitinib total: 20.4%, placebo: 4.3%). All acne events were Grades 1 or 2, and ≤ 0.5% of participants discontinued due to the event of acne. Acne is appropriately included as an ADR in SmPC section 4.8 with a frequency very common.

## Deaths

At the time of data cutoff, there were 4 TEAEs with fatal outcomes reported across the povorcitinib development program, none of them were considered by the investigator to be related to study drug. This is agreed.

## Serious adverse events

Across the pooled analyses, the incidence and pattern of serious TEAEs were generally low and comparable between treatment groups, with hidradenitis being the only SAE occurring in more than one participant. PC period: Few participants experienced serious TEAEs in the Phase 3 HS PC population (Pool 1, 14, 1.7% who took povorcitinib and 11, 2.7% who took placebo). The only serious TEAE reported for more than 1 participant in this population was hidradenitis 3 participants, 0.7%: povorcitinib 45-mg group and 2, 0.5% in the 75-mg group. Only hidradenitis and pneumonia AEs were considered to be study-drug related. Longer exposure: A total of 96 participants (6.8%) in the All HS Population experienced serious TEAEs. In all HS patient pool 2, the safety profile remained consistent with longer duration of exposure to povorcitinib. The most frequent serious TEAE was hidradenitis (PBO 1, 0.2%, total povorcitinib 21, 1.5%. In pool 2b study drug related serious TEAEs (10 participants) included hidradenitis (RT terms: RT terms: hospitalisation due to worsening HS, pain of bilateral axillae due to hidradenitis, and genital inflammatory abscesses due to HS) in 3 participants and anemia, faeces discolored, erysipelas, otitis externa, subcutaneous abscess, peripheral sensory neuropathy, paradoxical skin reaction each in 1 participant. Worsening of hidradenitis and serious infections are discussed above.

## Adverse Events Leading to Study Drug Discontinuation

PC period: The TEAEs leading to study drug discontinuation in participants in the Pool 1 was reported more frequently in the povorcitinib total group (N=31, 3.8%) than in the PBO group N=7, 1.7%). The TEAEs that led to study drug discontinuation in more than 1 participant included acne (3 participants in the povorcitinib 75-mg group) and ALT increased and anemia (2 participants each in the povorcitinib 45-mg group). All remaining TEAEs leading to study drug discontinuation were reported by no more than 1 participant each. Acne and elevated liver transaminases have both been identified as a povorcitinib-related ADRs in SmPC section 4.8. Long-term exposure: In Pool 2 the TEAEs leading to study drug discontinuation were reported more frequently in the total povorcitinib group (N=121, 8.5%) than in the PBO group (N=11, 2.4%). The most commonly reported TEAEs leading to study drug discontinuation in more than 2 participants who took povorcitinib included anemia, acne, ALT increased, hidradenitis, pulmonary embolism, transaminases increased, and weight increased. The TEAEs were similar as in the PC period, and anemia and ALT is discussed further under the below \"laboratory findings section\".

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

## Adverse Events Leading to Study Drug Interruption

In both pools with participants from the PC period (Pool 1) and participants with also longer exposure times (Pool 2) there were more drug interruptions among the povorcitinib participants: Pool 1 PBO N=24, 5.9%, total povorcitinib group N=58, 7.12%; Pool 2 PBO N=27, 5.8% total povorcitinib group N=262, 18.4%. The most frequent TEAEs leading to interruption of study drug in Pool 2 were blood creatine phosphokinase increased, COVID-19, anemia, herpes zoster, upper respiratory tract infection, ALT increased, hemoglobin decreased, AST increased, and hidradenitis. There were no new safety findings in this section, increased ALT and AST levels are further discussed above.

## Safety in special populations

Age, sex, race, ethnicity and geographical location: The possible effect of intrinsic factors, including age, sex, race, and ethnicity on the safety profile of povorcitinib was evaluated for the Phase 3 HS PC Population, the All HS Population, and the All povorcitinib Population. Overall, there were no meaningful differences in the exposure or TEAE profile of povorcitinib based on age, sex, race, ethnicity. Further, across all pools, there were no meaningful differences in the TEAE profile of povorcitinib based on geographic region. Limited exposure of patients over 65 years is noted, but the available data did not indicate specific safety concerns in elderly participants. In line with Art 20 referral for JAK inhibitors, lowest dose is recommended in elderly (see SmPC 4.2 and 4.4.). Pregnancy and lactation: No adequate and well-controlled studies of povorcitinib have been conducted in pregnant females to inform drug-associated risks. Females who were pregnant or lactating were excluded from all clinical studies. A total of 21 pregnancies have been reported across the povorcitinib clinical development program as of the data cutoff. The outcome of pregnancies varied, and some complications were also reported, including premature born baby, miscarriage and a baby born with 21 trisomy and talipes. Pregnancy is appropriately listed as a contraindication in SmPC section 4.3, in line with other products in the class. It is noted that 9/19 pregnancies (excluding two partner pregnancies) occurred in women using some form of oral contraception. Overall, in response to the question of whether an additional contraceptive method is warranted, the available data do not indicate that the drug compromises OC efficacy and therefore do not support mandatory dual contraception. However, given the occurrence of pregnancies among OC users, including cases without an identified alternative explanation, continued emphasis on correct and consistent OC use and appropriate precautions in situations that may compromise contraceptive effectiveness remains appropriate. Breast-feeding: No data are available regarding the presence of povorcitinib in human milk, the effects on the breast-fed child, or the effects on milk production. Breast-feeding is listed as a

contraindication in SmPC section 4.3, in line with other products in the class.

## Safety related to drug-drug interactions and other interactions

Povorcitinib is primarily cleared by CYP3A4 metabolism. A DDI study (INCB 54707-104) assessed the effect of an established CYP3A4 inhibitor (itraconazole) or inducer (rifampin) on the PK of povorcitinib.

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

Results showed that both itraconazole and rifampin had a significant impact on the PK of povorcitinib. For patients receiving chronic treatment with strong systemic CYP3A4 inhibitors, the recommended dose is 45 mg once daily (as outlined in SmPC section 4.2). Co-administration of povorcitinib with strong systemic CYP3A4 inducers is not recommended (as outlined in SmPC section 4.4).

Co-administration with oral contraceptives containing levonorgestrel and ethinyl estradiol did not result in clinically meaningful changes in exposure, supporting that no restrictions are required. Further, DDI studies found no clinically significant effect of povorcitinib on exposures of digoxin, rosuvastatin, and metformin as well as no clinically relevant impact of probenecid on povorcitinib exposure when they are coadministered.

## Clinical laboratory evaluations

## Clinical haematology

Hemoglobin: In Pool 1, treatment-emergent worsening to Grade 2 low haemoglobin occurred at similar frequencies with povorcitinib total and placebo (1.6% [13/821] vs 3.5% [14/405]), and Grade 3 worsening was rare (0.1% [1/821] overall; 0.2% [1/409] in the 75 mg group). Shifts from baseline Grade 0 to postbaseline Grade 2 occurred in 1 or 2 participants in each treatment group. There were no shifts from baseline Grade 0 or 1 to postbaseline Grade 3. For all treatment groups, the majority of participants with Grade 1 or 2 haemoglobin concentrations (low direction) postbaseline had low haemoglobin levels at baseline.

In the Pool 2, the overall pattern remained similar. While Grade 2 and Grade 3 low haemoglobin worsening was observed over longer exposure (Grade 2: 6.5% in povorcitinib total vs 3.7% in placebo; Grade 3: 1.0% in povorcitinib total), shift tables showed that progression from normal (Grade 0) to Grade 2 remained uncommon (≤2.4% in the 45 mg and 75 mg without dose change groups), and large worsening to Grade 3 with a ≥2-grade shift was very rare (4 participants total). Of note, cyclical changes in haemoglobin may confound the interpretation of low haemoglobin concentrations, particularly given that 62.7% of participants in the Phase 3 HS PC Population (Pool 1) were female (median age: 37.0 years). Additionally, elevated hsCRP levels, indicating a high inflammatory burden, can contribute to anaemia of inflammation. At present, there are no compelling evidence that lower hemoglobin levels are clearly drug-related and should be listed as ADRs. However, SmPC section 4.2 recommends interrupting treatment if Hb is &lt;8g/dL and that treatment may be restarted once Hb returns above this value.

Neutrophil counts: During PC period (Pool 1) there is a clear drop in the mean neutrophil counts of povorcitinib recipients compared to PBO at weeks 3 to 12. The mean neutrophil counts are most reduced in the povorcitinib 75mg group. In Pool 2, a total of 6 shifts to Grade 3 low neutrophils were observed (1 in the placebo groups and 5 in the povorcitinib groups). There were in total 3 participants with interruptions due to TEAEs of neutrophil count decreased or neutropenia (1 in the povorcitinib 45mg group and 2 in the povorcitinib 75-mg without dose change group), 1 participant had a recurrence of the event that led to study drug discontinuation. Aforementioned data collectively suggest that the lower neutrophil counts may be treatment-related and may have clinical significance. The applicant has appropriately listed neutropenia as ADR in SmPC 4.8 with description in the text and included relevant monitoring guidance in SmPC 4.2: Treatment should not be initiated and must be interrupted if ANC &lt; 1 × 10 3 /mm 3 . Treatment may be restarted once neutrophil count returns above this value.

Platelet Counts: The mean platelet counts were clearly reduced in povorcitinib participants during the placebo-controlled period (Weeks 3 to 12, Pool 1b). The most reduced values were observed in the 75 mg group at Week 3. In the all safety pools 1, 2 and 3, worsening to grade 2 or 3 were observed in the povorcitinib participants, but not in the PBO group. Treament-emergent reduction in platelet counts resulted in study interruptions. The applicant has included thrombocytopenia as an ADR in the SmPC 4.8 with description in the text. SmPC section 4.2 recommends to interrupt treatment if platelet counts are &lt; 50 × 109/L and that treatment may be restarted once platelet count returns above this value.

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

## Clinical chemistry

Creatinine/eGFR: Similar to other JAKis, treatment with povorcitinib led to modest, reversible eGFR decreases (incidence 30-42% across pools). Previous data show that the creatinine/eGFR changes during JAKi treatment are not associated with clinical renal function impairment. In Pool 1 PC period, eGFR worsening was similar between 45 mg and 75 mg (30.1% vs 30.8%). A majority of the events were mild and there were no severe events. There were no events of &gt; 3 × ULN or &gt; 3 × baseline increased creatinine. Acute kidney injuries were reported, but they were not considered related. No participants had treatment-emergent worsening to Grade 3 or 4 in Pool 1. The pattern across pools is most consistent with a class-related, modest, typically reversible change in creatinine/eGFR that is predominantly mild, with rare outliers with higher severity that are confounded by intercurrent illness and baseline risk factors.

Creatine Kinase: During the PC controlled period, in all HS patients (Pool 1), more participants who took povorcitinib had more treatment-emergent worsening to Grade 2 and 3 compared to PBO. In the pool with HS patients and longer exposure times (Pool 2) a total of 141 participants (10.9%) and 53 participants (4.1%) who took povorcitinib had treatment-emergent worsening to Grade 2 and 3, respectively. A total of 29 participants (2.2%) had worsening to Grade 4. The elevated creatine kinase levels were mostly transient and generally asymptomatic. They were not convincingly associated with rhabdomyolysis, myalgia or myositis. The elevated creatine kinase levels are appropriately identified as ADR in the SmPC section 4.8 with a frequency 'common'.

Liver aminotransferases: In Pool 1, both increased ALT &gt;3×ULN and AST &gt;3×ULN in were reported in 0.5% of the povorcitinib total group, compared with 0.0% and 0.2% in placebo, respectively. In Pool 2, increased ALT &gt;3×ULN was reported in 3.5% of the povorcitinib total group and increased AST &gt;3×ULN in 2.1%, compared with 0% and 0.2% on placebo, respectively. In Pool 3, increased ALT &gt;3×ULN occurred in 3.0% and increased AST &gt;3×ULN in 1.8% of participants in the povorcitinib total group.

As previously mentioned, the treatment-associated elevation of liver transaminases caused study drug interruptions and study discontinuations. Notably, one event of liver injury and one event of hepatic cytolysis were reported in the 45 mg group. Overall, ALT or AST (&gt;3×ULN) events occurred more frequently in povorcitinib groups compared to placebo group. The elevated liver transaminases are identified as an ADR for several other JAKis. The applicant has appropriately included elevated liver transferases as an ADR in SmPC 4.8 (\"Alanine aminotransferase increased &gt;3×ULN, uncommon\" and \"Aspartate aminotransferase increased &gt;3×ULN, uncommon).

Total cholesterol: In the Phase 3 HS Post-Anti-TNF PC Population (Pool 1b), the mean cholesterol levels increased from baseline to Week 6 in the povorcitinib groups and remained elevated until Week 12. Similar results as for the Pool 1b were observed for the Phase 3 HS PC Population (Pool 1). In the All HS Post-Anti-TNF Population (Pool 2b), the mean cholesterol levels also increased from baseline to Week 6 and then stabilised on an elevated level until Week 54. Similar results as in the Pool 2b were also observed in the All HS Population (Pool 2) and in the All povorcitinib Population (Pool 3). Also, higher triglyceride levels were seen more often in the povorcitinib participants; in the Pool1 the treatment emergent worsening to grade 2-4 was seen in 3.4% of PBO participants and in 4.8% of povorcitinib participants.

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

The applicant has included hyperlipidemia in SmPC 4.8 as ADRs with appropriate frequency and description in the text. SmPC 4.2 includes appropriate monitoring guidance: Patients should be monitored according to clinical guidelines for hyperlipidaemia.

## Adverse drug reactions in SmPC

The applicant considered the following factors were considered when making decisions on whether a causal relationship to povorcitinib in HS is plausible: Frequency of the event, TEAE rates seen with povorcitinib (45 mg and 75 mg) versus placebo, Biological plausibility based on povorcitinib mechanism of action and known effects of JAK inhibitor class, Population under study (including comorbidities and prior/concomitant therapy) and Incidence of Grade 3 or higher TEAEs, serious TEAEs, or TEAEs leading to study drug discontinuation. The analyses resulted in the identification of the following ADRs that have been appropriately included in the SmPC 4.8: upper respiratory tract infections (very common), acne (very common), folliculitis (common), urinary tract infection (common), hyperlipidaemia (common), headache (common), blood creatine phosphokinase increased (common), herpes zoster (uncommon), neutropenia (uncommon), thrombocytopenia (uncommon), Alanine aminotransferase increased &gt;3×ULN ( uncommon) and Aspartate aminotransferase increased &gt;3×ULN (uncommon).

## Note regarding the JAK inhibitor Art 20 referral

The PRAC concluded that, based on the currently available data, the increased risk for MACE, VTE, malignancy, serious infections and all-cause mortality observed in the ORAL Surveillance study with tofacitinib compared with TNF-inhibitors are considered JAKis class effects. The PRAC also concluded that these safety findings observed in patients with rheumatoid arthritis apply to all approved indications for the JAKis used in the treatment of chronic inflammatory disorders involved in the procedure.

To minimise these risks, the PRAC recommended implementing warnings for all JAKis included in the Art 20 review that these products should only be used in patients 65 years of age and older, who are current or past long-time smoker, with history of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease or other cardiovascular risk factors, or with other malignancy risk factors (e.g. current, or history of malignancy) if no suitable treatment alternatives are available. Cautious use is recommended in patients with known risk factors for VTE, other than those listed above.

The PRAC recommended to revise current dosing advice to lower the dose in certain patient groups with risk factors since the occurrence of MACEs, VTEs, malignancies, serious infections and all-cause mortality have been observed in a dose dependent manner.

The CHMP considers that those class effects also apply to Povofortay (povorcitinib), a JAK1 inhibitor and that these important safety concerns are also relevant for the HS indication. The Art 20 referral outcome (including the box warning, revised warnings, dose reduction in patients with RF) is thus fully applicable to povorcitinib.

## 5.4.12.2 Conclusions on clinical safety

Povorcitinib is JAK1 inhibitor. The size of the safety database is overall deemed sufficient and the pooling strategy appropriate. Overall, the safety profile of povorcitinib appears acceptable and consistent with known JAK inhibitor-associated risks, for both 45 mg and 75 mg dose. Regarding the Post-Anti-TNF subgroup, available data indicate that the safety profile does not differ substantially from the overall HS population.

Povorcitinib is contraindicated in active tuberculosis (TB) or active serious infections, pregnancy and breast feeding.

Povorcitinib was relatively well tolerated and has an acceptable safety profile in patients with HS. The safety profile of povorcitinib is appropriately reflected in the SmPC, which is adequately aligned with the previously identified JAK inhibitor class safety findings (Art. 20 referral).

## 6.1.2 Discussion on proposed safety specification

Herpes zoster: JAK 1 inhibition can impair antiviral defence mechanisms and predispose patients to reactivation of latent varicella zoster virus. The incidence rate of herpes zoster in patients treated with povorcitinib 45 mg was 2.2 per 100 patient-years, in patients treated with 75 mg was 3.3 per 100 patient-years, and in patients treated with placebo was 0 per 100 patient-years. The SmPC section 4.4 advises that if a patient develops herpes zoster, interruption of povorcitinib therapy should be considered until the episode resolves and recommends that patients are brought up to date with all immunisations, including prophylactic herpes zoster vaccinations. Proposed PL advises patients to monitor signs of herpes zoster. Inclusion of herpes zoster as important identified risk is endorsed by the CHMP and is in line with the safety specifications of other JAKis authorised for the treatment of chronic inflammatory disorders. Additional risk minimisation measures consisting of educational materials for health care providers and for patients and a post-authorisation safety study (PASS) to further characterise the risk have been included in the RMP.

Serious and opportunistic infections: Inhibition of JAK1 supresses immune surveillance and cellular immune response, increasing susceptibility to serious bacterial, fungal, viral, or opportunistic infections as well as reactivation of latent pathogens. In clinical trials, incidence rates of serious and opportunistic infections were either similar or lower in patients who took povorcitinib when compared with placebo. Inclusion of Serious and opportunistic infections as important potential risk is endorsed by the CHMP and is in line with the safety specifications of other JAKis authorised for the treatment of chronic inflammatory disorders. Active serious systemic infections, including active tuberculosis are contraindications according to the SmPC. Furthermore, the section 4.4. of the SmPC includes recommendations on appropriate clinical measures to reduce the risk of serious infections including tuberculosis and viral hepatitis. Additional risk minimisation measures consisting of educational materials for health care providers and for patients and a PASS study to further characterise this risk have been included in the RMP.

## Malignancy (excluding non-melanoma skin cancer) and non-melanoma skin cancer:

Malignancies, including non-melanoma skin cancer (NMSC), have been reported in patients receiving JAKis. In a large randomised active-controlled study of tofacitinib (ORAL Surveillance) in RA patients ≥ 50 years of age with underlying CV risk factors, a higher rate of malignancies, particularly lung cancer, lymphoma and NMSC, was observed with tofacitinib compared to TNF inhibitors. Approved therapies in the JAKi class are being investigated for potential risk of malignancies and include additional risk minimisation measures for these risks. Inclusion of Malignancy (excluding non-melanoma skin cancer) and non-melanoma skin cancer as separate important potential risks is endorsed by the CHMP and is in line with the safety specifications of other JAKis. povorcitinib SmPC section 4.4 specifies patient populations for which povorcitinib should only be used if no suitable treatment alternatives are available and advises on periodic skin examination. Additional risk minimisation measures to manage the risk of malignancies and a PASS study to further characterise the risk of malignancies have been included in the RMP.

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

Embryofoetal toxicity following exposure in utero: The JAK-STAT pathway is known to be involved in early embryonic development and other approved JAKis include embryo-foetal toxicity following exposure in utero as important potential risk with additional risk minimisation measures in their RMPs. Studies in animals have shown reproductive toxicity: povorcitinib has been shown to cause decreased embryofoetal survival (post- implantation loss) and decreased foetal weight in pregnant rats and rabbits. povorcitinib is therefore contraindicated during pregnancy and is not recommended in women of childbearing potential not using contraception. Women of childbearing potential have to use effective contraception during treatment with povorcitinib and for at least 4 weeks after the last dose in. Inclusion of Embryofoetal toxicity following exposure in utero as important potential risk is endorsed. Additional risk minimisation measures to manage the risk have been included in the RMP.

Regarding breastfeeding, in a pre-and postnatal development study in rats, females were administered povorcitinib at doses of 3, 10, or 25 mg/kg per day from GD 6 through LD 21. Several females dosed at 25 mg/kg/day had clinical observations consistent with dystocia beginning on GD 20 and were euthanised. A decrease in number of pups born, pup birth weight, postnatal survival, and body weight gain was observed at this dose, and beginning on PND 10, observations of limited usage of fore and hindlimbs were observed resulting in early termination of this group on PND 21. These clinical observations correlated to necropsy findings of malrotated paws and skeletal variations of bent or misshapen limb bones. Similar findings were not observed in the doses of 3 or 10 mg/kg/day. Based on the absence of skeletal findings in the embryo-foetal development study, these findings likely occurred during the postnatal period via lactational exposure. Povorcitinib exposure was confirmed in pups during the lactation period. Since a risk to newborns/infants cannot be excluded, breastfeeding is contraindicated in povorcitinib SmPC section 4.3. As breastfeeding is a contraindication and the claimed indication does not include paediatric patients, the potential risk of impaired bone development needs not to be addressed as a safety concern in the RMP.

Long-term safety: In line with the safety specification of other JAKis the applicant has included Longterm safety as missing information in the RMP. HS is a chronic disease requiring long-term treatment, therefore further characterisation of long-term safety profile is needed for events with low frequency and long latency. Long-term safety is addressed in the pharmacovigilance plan. Inclusion of Long-term safety as missing information is endorsed.

MACE and Venous thromboembolism (including DVT and PE): Approved therapies in the JAKi class are being investigated for the potential risk of MACE and venous thromboembolism. In a large randomised active-controlled study of tofacitinib (another JAK inhibitor) in rheumatoid arthritis patients 50 years and older with at least one additional cardiovascular risk factor, a higher rate of MACE, defined as cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction and non-fatal stroke and a dose dependent higher rate of venous thromboembolism including deep venous thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE) was observed with tofacitinib compared to TNF inhibitors. Events of MACE, deep venous thrombosis and pulmonary embolism have been reported in povorcitinib clinical trials. MACE and venous thromboembolism have the potential to impact the risk-benefit profile as these events, though infrequent, may be life-threatening or fatal. Inclusion of MACE and venous thromboembolism (including DVT and PE) as separate important potential risks in the RMP is endorsed by the CHMP and is in line other JAKis authorised for the treatment of chronic inflammatory disorders.

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

Additional risk minimisation measures to manage the risk of MACE and Venous thromboembolism and a PASS study to further characterise these risks have been included in the RMP.

Gastrointestinal perforation (GIP): is included as a safety concern in RMPs of several, but not all approved JAKis. GIPs have been identified in pivotal clinical trials of JAKis in RA patients, with additional cases reported in subsequent long-term extension studies. Concomitant treatment with steroids or NSAIDs is a significant risk factor for GIP reporting. Consequently, these findings have led the FDA to recommend cautious use of JAKis in patients at risk for GIP, such as patients with a history of diverticulitis or peptic ulcer disease, and in patients receiving concurrent treatment with steroids or NSAIDs. In povorcitinib clinical trials there was one serious event of diverticulitis intestinal perforated (and one event of cutaneous abscess miscoded as GI-perforation) observed. HS is not independently recognised as a risk factor for GI perforation. Given the rarity of the events and the younger demographic profile of patients with HS who generally have a lower baseline prevalence of the risk factors for GI perforation, the applicant agreed to closely monitor GI perforation in future PSURs and update the RMP in the post-marketing setting as appropriate based on emerging post-marketing data.

Other risks proposed not to be included in the list of safety concerns in the RMP: The applicant's justification for non-inclusion of Blood creatine phosphokinase increased, Upper respiratory tract infections, Acne, and Folliculitis as important risks in the RMP is supported. These risks are adequately addressed in the product information and do not require additional pharmacovigilance or risk minimisation activities. Monitoring of these risks via routine pharmacovigilance activities is considered sufficient.

## 6.2.2 Discussion on the pharmacovigilance plan

## 6.2.2.1 Routine pharmacovigilance activities

The applicant does not propose any other routine pharmacovigilance activities beyond adverse events reporting and signal detection which is agreed. In addition, and upon request, the applicant agreed to closely monitor 'Gastrointestinal perforation' in future PSURs.

<div style=\"page-break-after: always\"></div>

Routine pharmacovigilance is nevertheless not considered sufficient, and additional activities are warranted, as discussed below.

## 6.2.2.2 Additional pharmacovigilance activities

Upon request, the applicant proposed one extension study INCB 54707-312 to collect long-term safety data, which is included in the safety concerns as missing information. Study INCB 54707-312 (EU CT: 2023-507204-31-00) is an extension study with participants from the two main phase 3 clinical trials supporting the MAA, with an additional 52 weeks of follow-up. 'Long-term safety' will be assessed through systematic and structured collection and analysis of adverse events. Adverse events of special interest (AESIs) will be actively monitored throughout the study and will be documented using dedicated electronic case report form. The AESIs include 'serious infections', 'opportunistic infections, 'herpes zoster', 'tuberculosis', 'malignancy (all types)', 'cardiovascular events (eg, major adverse cardiovascular events [MACE])', and 'other embolic and thrombotic events (eg, pulmonary embolism, deep vein thrombosis, thrombosis, cerebrovascular events)'. These selected AESIS are in line with the list of safety concerns.

The number of patients yet recruited in the long-term study (i.e. 617) is considered low. Even if the goal of recruitment is reached, it is not considered sufficiently large to detect uncommon or rare adverse events. Additionally, events (e.g., MACE, malignancy) may have a long TTO, also beyond the intended follow-up time of the extension studies. Therefore, additional PhV activities are needed to further characterise the risks of povorcitinib in the post-marketing setting. The applicant has thus proposed to conduct a PASS for povorcitinib to provide long-term safety data and further characterise the safety concerns: 'Long-term safety, 'herpes zoster', 'serious and opportunistic infections', 'VTE (including DVT and PE)', 'MACE', 'malignancy (excluding non-melanoma skin cancer)' and 'nonmelanoma skin cancer'. Additionally, 'all-cause mortality' was included as an endpoint of the PASS in line with the Article 20 referral on JAKIs authorised for the treatment of chronic inflammatory disorders. The study is proposed to comprise multiple datasets and include both European and North American patients. Protocol submission, alongside a full feasibility assessment, should be submitted in June 2027, with data collection starting in November 2027. The duration of the study is 5 years, with interim reports submitted yearly. These milestones are accepted.

The applicant will also implement a drug utilisation study (DUS) to evaluate the effectiveness of the risk minimisation measures implemented within the EMA Article 20 referral for JAK inhibitors. The study will be a descriptive analysis of HS patients in Europe, with a 2-year study period. The protocol should be submitted in June 2027, with data collection starting in November 2027, which is acceptable.

## 6.4.2 Discussion on the risk minimisation measures

## 6.4.2.1 Routine risk minimisation measures

The proposed routine risk minimisation measures are considered appropriate by the PRAC. Nevertheless, additional risk minimisation measures were deemed warranted, as discussed below.

## 6.4.2.2 Additional risk minimisation measures

JAKis for chronic inflammatory disorders may cause serious side effects, and additional measures to minimise these risks are thus warranted, as concluded in the referral for the class of JAKis (EMA/142279/2023). Awareness and knowledge of patients and prescribers of the safety concerns is critical to help mitigate important risks, enable prompt management of adverse events and ensure optimal use of povorcitinib. This requires measures beyond routine risk minimisation measures.

The applicant has therefore proposed additional risk minimisation measures for povorcitinib which will consist of educational material for health care professionals (HCP guide) and patients (patient card), addressing the important identified risks and important potential risks in line with the agreed list of safety concerns: herpes zoster, serious and opportunistic infections, malignancy (excluding nonmelanoma skin cancer), non-melanoma skin cancer, embryo-foetal toxicity following exposure in utero, MACE and venous Thromboembolism (including DVT and PE).

In addition, the current SmPC section 4.3 includes a contraindication for use during pregnancy. Further, the SmPC section 4.6 includes advice that effective contraceptives should be used by women of childbearing potential for 4 weeks after cessation of treatment with povorcitinib. Considering the longterm treatment with povorcitinib, risk awareness beyond the initial prescription is considered needed as the compliance with the contraindication may be reduced with repeated prescription. Based on the current evidence, a negative effect on embryofetal development cannot be excluded and as such further guidance directed beyond the information included in the SmPC and the PL is needed. Thus, the applicant has included additional riks minimisation measures (i.e. HCP guide and a patient card) also for the important potential risk 'embryofoetal toxicity following exposure in utero'. This is agreed.

The format of the aRMMs is accepted. A description of the content of the materials with key elements is included in the RMP Annex 6 and correspondingly in the SmPC Annex IID.

## 6.5 RMP summary and RMP annexes overall conclusion

The RMP Part VI and the RMP Annexes are acceptable.

## 6.6 Overall conclusion on the Risk Management Plan

The CHMP and PRAC consider that the risk management plan version 1.0 is acceptable.
